items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: Noble Sissel carried a wonderful band over there. A wonderful band over there. Twelve pieces.

ctx.x: Some people talk like Europe introduced jazz to Europe, that is James Europe's band, because they would jazz up numbers. Do you know anything about that?

I wouldn't doubt it. I wouldn't doubt it. I wouldn't say that he didn't. I would say that the first acclaim the Frenchman's really give to anyone for the introduction of jazz over there came through and by the efforts of James Reese Europe. Other than, uh, than after James Reese Europe left the scene, after he was killed, I'll say that the furtherance of this was caused by Noble Sissel. And Noble Sissel carried a wonderful band over there. A wonderful band over there. Twelve pieces. I think Noble Sissel carried…
Sidney Bechet was over there about the time of the war, too.
